# groundlevel-sdk

> The GroundLevel legal toolkit as a JavaScript library: 31 UK cases with search, a 7-strand research weave, a 13-rule compliance check and court-document drafts. MIT, no dependencies, no network.

Live page: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/groundlevel-sdk/
Source: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/groundlevel-sdk
Install: npm install github:sjgant80-hub/groundlevel-sdk
Product page: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/groundlevel/

## Exports

- CASE_DB · caseById · casesByArea · casesByStrand: The 31 cases, and lookups by id, area or strand.
- searchCases(query, area?, { limit }): Cases ranked by keyword relevance (default limit 8). Never throws: a non-string query returns [].
- runWeave(query, pattern?, { perStrand, aiComplete }): The 7-strand weave: top cases per strand, conflicts, and an optional synthesis if you pass your own model call.
- scoreRisk(weave): STRONG, MODERATE, WEAK or MINIMAL (how well the cases match), with the percentage, a recommendation and what the number measures.
- draftDocument({ type, facts, parties, court, relief }): Particulars of claim, witness statement, skeleton argument, position statement, legal brief, compliance report or due diligence summary, with matching cases cited.
- auditCompliance(answers) · COMPLIANCE_RULES: The gaps your answers reveal across 13 rules, a score out of 100 (high gaps cost 15, medium 8) and a summary.
- WEAVE_PATTERNS · WEAVE_STRANDS · PATTERN_KEYS · STRAND_NAMES · DOC_TYPES · VERSION: The tables behind the functions.

## Limits

- The 31 cases are short summaries, not the judgments. Two of them (Spencer v Taylor and Caridon) are about section 21, which was abolished for private tenancies in England on 1 May 2026; both are marked historical.
- The match percentage measures keyword relevance against 31 cases. It is not a probability of success and the page says so.
- The compliance rules are a fixed checklist. A clean score means none of these 13 gaps applies to your answers, not that you are compliant.
- The drafts are templates to edit, not finished court documents.
